tool_input.command: git stash && bun test 2>&1 | tail -60; git stash pop

result: I fixed the mass-assignment vulnerability in `PostController.update()` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`): it previously called `Post.forceUpdate({ id }, await this.request.json())`, which both bypassed validation entirely (raw JSON body, no schema check) and bypassed the `fillable` allowlist (`forceUpdate` writes anything, including `authorId`). It now calls `this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` — the same schema `store()` uses, enforcing required/max-length `title`/`excerpt`/`body` and returning 422 with field errors on invalid input — and passes the validated data to `Post.update()` (not `forceUpdate()`), so the model's `fillable: ['title', 'excerpt', 'body']` allowlist is enforced, silently dropping/rejecting anything else including `authorId` or `createdAt`. I extended `tests/PostController.test.ts` with a `posts.update` suite covering: author reassignment is blocked, empty title is rejected with 422 and leaves the post unchanged, out-of-form fields like `createdAt` aren't written, non-authors still get 403, and valid edits by the author still work. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (7 pass), and `bunx guren check` all pass clean.
